newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse ends lower, seen rebounding soon.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse ends lower, seen rebounding soon.

text.p: Greek stocks closed 0.74 percent lower on Thursday on moderate volume with analysts saying the market was correcting in profit taking and expecting it will regain momentum next week.

"The market corrected on Thursday, a necessary movement before a new rise. By next week, the index is likely to recover and this could start even on Friday if corrections occur during the session. Market sentiment is good," said Maria Lentziou, an analyst at Olympic Securities.
Volume was moderate at 8.9 billion drachmas and indicated a relatively mild selling interest, she said.
The index will stabilise around 1,070-1,080 points, before it mounts again and the banking sector will continue to lead the way, Lentziou added.
Other interesting investment opportunities exist in metallurgical and aluminium companies which have good prospects in 1997, she said.
Another broker said the correction was reasonable and the market would recover next week.

"The correction may continue on Friday but we will see a recovery next week. The index will not go lower than 1,050 points and will stabilise at that level, before it rises again," said Tassos Stamatopoulos, managing director at Kyklos Securities.
The market had momentum and the corrections should not cause any concern, he added.
The Athens general share index closed 0.74 percent or 8.07 points down at 1080.43 from Wednesday's 1088.50, after opening at 1087.40.

Most sectoral indices were down with banks losing 1.26 percent, construction dropping 1.36 percent and investment shares ending 1.29 percent down. Small caps ended 0.90 percent down but industrials gained 0.42 percent.
Thursday's turnover was moderate at 8.9 billion drachmas on volume of 2.8 million shares. Losers led gainers 143 to 71 with 27 issues unchanged on 241 traded.
